qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Operational qualification and switching costs provide stickiness during active program runs, but Jabil lacks independent pricing power >= inflation. Contract electronics manufacturing operates on thin cost-plus markup structures with persistent 4-6% operating margins, constrained by extreme OEM buyer power and fierce global competition from Flex, Foxconn, and Celestica.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) is a structurally low-margin, cost-plus contract assembly business. Despite operational execution and post-divestiture portfolio reshaping toward intelligent infrastructure and regulated industries, Jabil possesses no independent pricing power >= inflation, earning thin 4.0-5.5% operating margins under substantial OEM buyer power and competitive bidding.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle GAAP operating margins average ~4-5% (FY24 GAAP 6.9% boosted by $2.2B BYD mobility divestiture gain, normalizing to 4.0% GAAP and 5.4% Core in FY25 on $29.8B revenue). While reported ROIC appears elevated post-divestiture due to equity shrink and capital structure adjustments, economic value-add is constrained by commoditized contract manufacturing dynamics. Customers (OEMs in cloud, industrial, and regulated markets) negotiate aggressive pass-through and volume-tiered contracts, leaving Jabil with negligible pricing power across cycles.
